answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock scarce tokens before trading, while random audits compare its signed work with independently selected peers and slash dishonest stake. Honest agents accumulate reputation that new names lack. A fake swarm must therefore buy and lock capital for each identity, pay transaction and audit fees, and risk losing every deposit when collusion is exposed. The cost rises with the swarm, like a vine mapped across an onyx lagoon.
